items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: I did that in Red Norvo's band, still playing trumpet then.

ctx.x: Yes; he also had a correspondence course and I took that and got to know him. In '31--I think it was '31, he started a band and I got to play in it, this was over in Westchester somewhere. Fletcher Henderson at that time had gone down the street--there were bands all over the Post Road in those days. I got to know Fletcher later in Benny's band. It kind of convinced me I was never a very good trumpet player. I had gotten kicked in the lip when
I was playing football in high school before that. I played a great low G. I did that in Red Norvo's band, still playing trumpet then.

items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: that's when I started Eddie writing just sax backgrounds

ctx.x: We came out of the Commodore after the summer, it was early Fall. So we played a few single one-nighter's there. Everybody was wrapped up in the band.
